SEED (Mark Builds Brands, "1 product. 3 AI tools. I make $23K/day", 2025-07-09): "Purple ocean strategy": enter a market that is already hot and validated, then carve out a micro-market for a specific group of people. Primal Queen sells beef-organ supplements specifically to women who are postpartum and perimenopausal — "two of the most significant events in the life of women biologically speaking." Hims and Hers split GLP-1 weight loss by gender because "women and men just view their health completely differently... we have completely different hormone structures." A hydrogen-water bottle brand is scaling by selling the bottle on a skin-quality angle: "the quality of water that you drink is going to impact acne that you have on your face, the blemishes, the imperfections." Margin rules: $20 gross margin and 3x cost of goods; "humans buy based off emotion and then they justify with logic"; "all of marketing at its core is simply a game of belief change work"; "perception of value" is half the sale.

LATENT INTERPRETATION (understand): Beneath the marketing talk is a consumer tension: people inside a biological transition they did not choose — postpartum recovery, perimenopause, mid-life male metabolism, adult acne-prone skin — feel that generic health regimes were not built for the body they now have. The aspiration is to regain a sense of authorship over that body: to have the everyday ritual objects of a health regime (what they swallow, drink, apply) recognize their specific state and constraints, and to be told by a peer voice rather than a clinic that their situation is normal and addressable. The capacity being served is self-knowledge during transition; the tension is between a mass-market product's implicit "average adult" and a self that no longer feels average. Communities where this is lived: r/Menopause and perimenopause groups, postpartum and "fourth trimester" forums, animal-based and carnivore diet communities, adult-acne and skincare subreddits, GLP-1 patient communities (semaglutide/tirzepatide forums), hydration/"water quality" hobbyist groups.
